title: Empty Object Pool Checkout Error Instead of Allocation
pattern: A reuse cache or object pool whose items are ordinary, cheaply constructible values returns an error or throws when no cached item is available, instead of constructing a new one.
why_bad: Cache depletion is an expected state, not a failure. Returning `Exhausted` forces every caller to catch the error and construct the resource manually, duplicating the pool's own construction logic and defeating the point of the abstraction.
detection: A pool/cache getter that checks `available.is_empty()` (or equivalent) and returns `Err`/throws without attempting to construct a new item, where the item type has a plain constructor and the pool's size is not a capacity limit.
counterexample: Pools whose bound is a capacity control: database connections, threads, file descriptors, GPU buffers, or fixed hardware resources. There, exhaustion must block with a timeout or fail fast, and silently growing the pool is a resource-capacity bug.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring*, "Replace Exception with Test", pp. 620–622.
